description:
Why Does Pluto's Moon Have a Red Cap Called Mordor?

Episode 105 of a daily journey through the universe. 🔴
We visit Charon, Pluto's biggest moon: discovered in 1978, about 1,212 km wide, half the size of Pluto, the two locked face to face, a giant canyon belt, and a red north pole nicknamed Mordor Macula, colored by gas stolen from Pluto.

➡️ Tomorrow, Episode 106: Next stop, Eris. The dwarf planet that got Pluto demoted.

segments.text: Why does Pluto's moon have a red cap, nicknamed Mordor?
In nineteen seventy-eight, astronomer James Christy noticed a bump on blurry photos of Pluto. It was a moon.
segments.headline: Discovered in 1978

segments.text: Charon is about one thousand two hundred kilometers wide. Half the size of Pluto.
It's so big that Pluto and Charon orbit a point in the empty space between them. Like two dancers holding hands.
segments.headline: Dancing partners

segments.text: And they always show each other the same face. From one side of Pluto, Charon never rises, and never sets.
In twenty fifteen, New Horizons flew past and saw canyons longer than the Grand Canyon, maybe from an ancient frozen ocean.
segments.headline: Giant canyons

segments.text: And a strange red cap at its north pole. Scientists nicknamed it Mordor.
segments.headline: Mordor

segments.text: The red comes from Pluto. Gas escapes Pluto, freezes on Charon's cold pole, and sunlight turns it red.
segments.headline: Painted by Pluto

segments.text: A moon painted by its own planet.
